rationale: Both reviews are grounded and actionable, covering the enum/test-coverage themes from the human thread and adding solid original findings (X's default-level footgun, Y's concurrency race and tag-validation gaps). The deciding factor is the latent gap check: Y explicitly names five existing hardware tests that already do sleep(level=2)+wake_up and will now hit the new NotImplementedError, directly matching the real-world outcome (issue #4905/#4912) that the strict guard was too strict and had to be relaxed — X's related finding (default level=2 'bricks' fresh usage) is adjacent but frames it as an ergonomics footgun rather than identifying it breaks pre-existing tests/CI, so it doesn't clearly hit the gap. Y's deeper cross-file verification (diffusion_worker.py level-2 restore path, docs) also gives it a modest recall/actionability edge.
